docs.text: Introduction to IBM Bob What is IBM Bob? IBM Bob is an AI-powered software development lifecycle (SDLC) partner that integrates directly into the development environment. Bob operates across the full development lifecycle — not just as a code generator, but as a partner that supports planning, implementation, and automation throughout a project. Bob's core capabilities: Code writing and modification : Writes new code and modifies existing code across the entire codebase based on natural language instructions Codebase understanding : Reads and reasons about complex project structures, dependencies, and architectural patterns Development task automation : Automates repetitive tasks such as documentation, commit message generation, and test scaffolding Bob as an SDLC Partner The distinction between Bob and a traditional code generator is scope. Bob is designed to support the entire software development lifecycle, not just the moment of writing a function or fixing a bug. This includes: Helping plan features before implementation begins Understanding the full context of a project before making changes Keeping the developer in control at every step Bob augments existing workflows rather than replacing developer judgment. Interfaces Bob is available in two primary form factors: Interface Description Bob IDE VS Code extension providing an agentic sidebar, inline code assistance, and mode-based interaction Bob Shell Terminal-based interface offering the same capabilities in a keyboard-driven, automation-friendly form factor Learning Path Structure This learning path covers IBM Bob across five chapters: Chapter Focus 1 Demo setup and environment introduction 2 Core interaction patterns: tab completion, next edit prediction, and the agentic chat 3 Customization: project context, custom rules, and custom modes 4 Advanced topics: context window management and Bob Shell 5 Extending Bob's capabilities with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) Each chapter builds on the previous, progressing from basic interactions to advanced configuration and integration. Key Takeaways Bob supports the full software development lifecycle, not just code generation Two interfaces are available: Bob IDE (VS Code) and Bob Shell (terminal) The developer remains in control — Bob assists with reasoning and implementation, but does not replace developer judgment This learning path progresses from beginner to advanced topics across five chapters
